requirements.text: Decode declared schema versions and preserve event identity and event time.
Compute half-open tumbling sums/counts and quarantine excessively late events.
Bound memory, spill deterministically and commit progress with state/output.

problem.scope: Finite events carry explicit event timestamps and schema-version transitions. Compare incremental keyed event-time state with immutable microbatch recomputation. Watermarks express a lateness policy; bounded memory/spill and replay are explicit.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

acceptanceCases.given: A 10ms tumbling window sees timestamps 9,10, a duplicate ID, and a timestamp below watermark 5.
acceptanceCases.then: Time 9 maps to [0,10), time 10 to [10,20); the duplicate is ignored and timestamp 4 quarantined.
acceptanceCases.when: Apply mixed-schema canonical values to the bounded window fold.

acceptanceCases.given: An event lands exactly at a tumbling-window boundary.
acceptanceCases.then: Assign the event to the new half-open window, independent of arrival order.
acceptanceCases.when: Decode its version and compute floor(eventTime/width).

acceptanceCases.given: Watermark is 5 and events at 4 and 5 arrive.
acceptanceCases.then: Quarantine time 4 and allow time 5; idle partitions must follow an explicit policy.
acceptanceCases.when: Classify both under the declared event-time policy.

acceptanceCases.given: A worker crashes after output is written but before source checkpoint commit.
acceptanceCases.then: Deduplicate or reconcile versioned output so sum/count do not double; unknown schema versions remain quarantined.
acceptanceCases.when: Restore and replay the same event identities.

guarantees: The code states the bounded decision rule; unimplemented helpers remain pseudocode.
External effects, distributed failure and latency require separate execution evidence.
Restore a checkpoint, deduplicate replayed IDs and publish versioned window results; finality follows the declared watermark rule.
